review.reviewer: Codex implementation owner, design self-review; not independent approval
review.decision: Close four precise standalone refresh review boundaries without widening write authority
review.notes: Independent Q report/manifest fully read and SHA checked. Preserve HQR001..006 and original Q/failed evidence. Pre-scan exact standalone marker before parser value consumption and actions. Keep backup fd for bounded content verification; no-follow recheck current leaf inode, and conservatively leave any failed/changed backup instead of unlinking an uncertain path. Detect recognized external user/knowledge blocks and unknown content after the generated LOCAL boundary, refuse safely rather than silently remove effective instructions or auto-migrate. Use a dedicated single-link private lock open that checks nlink before chmod while preserving existing regular/owner/no-follow/managed-parent checks and normal flock. Backup legacy helper and generic private primitives are inherited; state precisely what this new caller makes reachable. Keep best-effort external editor conflict boundary and post-rename fsync limits, not an artificial CAS guarantee. Exact old-Q controls for parser/mixed content/hardlink and a declared old-logic plus observer backup control precede green. No real HQ/config/KB/session/permissions changes.

cases.description: Malformed value flags cannot swallow standalone refresh
cases.setup: Use actual CmdHQ and recording rejecting tmux in synthetic HOME; value-taking flags before/after the standalone marker, missing values and help.
cases.expected: Standalone marker is validated before value consumption/actions; every incompatible combination exits2 without seed/enroll/launch/tmux/writes. Ordinary legitimate agent/language values and existing read-only help semantics remain.

cases.description: Backup verification and failure never remove a replacement object
cases.setup: Actual exclusive backup writer with a deterministic after-write observer replacing the path with a same-UID file, symlink or FIFO, plus ordinary backup and collision controls.
cases.action: Verify the created fd and current path identity under the observer-controlled ordering.
cases.expected: Bounded no-follow verification returns conflict for changed identity; source and replacement bytes/inode remain, no unlink of an uncertain path, no blocking FIFO or arbitrary reads. A failed partial owned backup may remain visibly retained. Negative control reintroduces old path-read/unlink semantics at the same seam; not claimed old-binary concurrency.

cases.description: Mixed active instruction blocks are not silently overwritten
cases.setup: Managed old en/zh files with independent user and valid knowledge blocks before/after LOCAL, arbitrary trailing instructions, and canonical managed-only controls.
cases.action: Invoke standalone refresh and compare all file bytes/mtime/backups.
cases.expected: Conservatively reject recognized external blocks or unknown post-LOCAL content without modifying original/LOCAL/knowledge; do not migrate private content automatically. Canonical managed-only files still upgrade with verified backup. Same/future-version limits remain honest.

cases.description: The shared apply lock rejects hardlinked leaves before chmod
cases.setup: Actual standalone Cmd and lock acquisition with isolated managed root and external same-UID0644 sentinel hardlinked as lock; owner/no-follow/single-link contention controls.
cases.action: Try refresh and compare external inode/mode/content/mtime; then use ordinary lock and contend.
cases.expected: Hardlink is rejected before mode/truncate changes, preserving external file and rules. Normal single-link private lock retains flock/owner/parent protections; no global weakening of private IO. Tests never change real permissions.
